prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "image", with the standing line "Turns a built prompt into a saved, annotated picture, checking the model and recording every paid call." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A single left-to-right channel. At left, two stacked sheets of text feed together into one funnel: the technical prompt above, the enhanced prompt below, joined by a blank line. The funnel passes through a gate plate stamped with a checkmark for accepted models and a barred slot for rejected ones. Beyond the gate the channel widens into a sizing frame that reshapes to square, wide, or tall. A key-shaped token enters the channel from below before the gate; if absent, a side chute diverts to an empty file. From the gate the channel runs to a remote cloud provider and returns carrying bytes, splitting into two paths: one writes a file, one drops a coin into a ledger drawer.

Magnified circles set beside it show top circle, the sizing frame showing three empty rectangles, square, wide, tall, chosen by words found in the prompt. middle circle, the returned response holding both a link and packed bytes, with the link taking precedence. bottom circle, the ledger drawer receiving one row per successful response, with blank fields when usage is missing.

Colour is used so that warm ochre marks the prompt text and its assembly. Deep teal marks the checked model and the paid request. Muted red marks refusals, missing credentials, and logged-only failures.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 2 prompts combined into 1; 3 sizes selected from the prompt text; 1 ledger row per successful response; annotation occupies the bottom fifth of the picture; 1 attempt, no retries.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: gpt-image-2 on the gate plate; image_wait and image_download on the progress steps; annotate on the lettering step; terse prompt on the text burned at the foot; generated and annotated on the two output folders; .png on the saved file.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: technical prompt, enhanced prompt, final prompt, model check, gpt-image-2, unsupported model, api key, empty placeholder, image timeout, generated bytes 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, url or bytes, one ledger row image_wait, image_download, annotate, terse prompt, bottom strip generated, annotated, .png file, opened locally no substitution, failures logged

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Two prompts join, blank line between; Unknown model fails before any paid request; No key writes an empty file Link wins when both are returned; Zero usage prints as zero Terse prompt is burned along the foot A write failure still leaves the call counted A ledger error never discards the picture
